scenario: [LGRA.23.2]: a kwarg may be declared with an opaque type ([LOPQ.3.2]), and "a kwarg declared with an opaque type takes no `default`, because no literal has an opaque type ([LOPQ.3.3])". Library `crypto` declares `opaque type Key over Bytes`; a service declares `kwarg k: Key default "ab"`. It is refused with DS_VALIDATE_SERVICE_KWARG_DEFAULT_TYPE, though the kwarg type itself is legal (`compiler/LOPQ.3.2`) and a String literal is one the parser takes after `default`. PATH PINNED: `lgra_23_2_default_misfit`'s `te_opaque(_)` arm, in dsc.validate. Without it the program compiles and the encoder writes `has_default` with an empty `default_value`.
rules_ds:
from crypto import Key

service svc.sign:
    kwarg k: Key default "ab"
    no response
